entries.content_plain: CHAPTER (ELEGY) 3 La 3:1-66 . Jeremiah proposes his own experience under afflictions, as an example as to how the Jews should behave under theirs, so as to have hope of a restoration; hence the change from singular to plural ( La 3:22 , 40-47 ). The stanzas consist of three lines, each of which begins with the same Hebrew letter. Aleph. 1-3. seen affliction-- his own in the dungeon of Malchiah ( Jr 38:6 ); that of his countrymen also in the siege. Both were types of that of Christ.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10866"/><div sID="gen19542" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10866"/>34-36. This triplet has an infinitive in the beginning of each verse, the governing finite verb being in the end of <reference osisRef="Lam.3.36">La 3:36</reference>, "the Lord approveth not," which is to be repeated in each verse. Jeremiah here anticipates and answers the objections which the Jews might start, that it was by His connivance they were "crushed under the feet" of those who "turned aside the right of a man." God approves (literally, "seeth," <reference osisRef="Hab.1.13">Ha 1:13</reference>; so "behold," "look on," that is, look on with approval) not of such unrighteous acts; and so the Jews may look for deliverance and the punishment of their foes. <div eID="gen19542" type="x-p"/>
